links.outcome: Information quality and guideline concordance of retrieval-augmented vs non-retrieval LLMs on hemodialysis questions
links.effect: RAG-based models (Perplexity, Copilot) showed relatively higher information reliability and better guideline alignment; non-retrieval models more often omitted guideline-recommended elements or were less specific.
links.quote: RAG-based models also showed relatively better alignment with reference guideline statements, whereas non-retrieval-based models more often omitted guideline-recommended elements or provided less specific responses.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM outputs versus recommended sixth-grade benchmark
links.effect: None of the outputs met the recommended sixth-grade readability benchmark; greater guideline concordance was often accompanied by higher linguistic complexity.
links.quote: None of the outputs met the recommended sixth-grade readability benchmark, and greater guideline concordance was often accompanied by higher linguistic complexity.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated patient education text
links.effect: No output met the sixth-grade readability benchmark across FKGL, FRES, GFI, CLI, and SMOG metrics.
links.quote: None of the outputs met the recommended sixth-grade readability benchmark, and greater guideline concordance was often accompanied by higher linguistic complexity.

links.outcome: Guideline concordance and omissions of guideline-recommended elements in LLM outputs
links.effect: Non-retrieval models often omitted guideline-recommended elements or gave less specific responses versus KDIGO-based reference statements; RAG models aligned relatively better.
links.quote: RAG-based models also showed relatively better alignment with reference guideline statements, whereas non-retrieval-based models more often omitted guideline-recommended elements or provided less specific responses.

links.outcome: Hallucinations and unsafe recommendations in LLM outputs for hemodialysis patients
links.effect: Qualitative review found medical hallucinations: contraindicated self-management suggestions, potentially inappropriate dietary advice, and out-of-scope clinical instructions presented as self-care.
links.quote: Qualitative review identified several examples of model-generated "medical hallucinations," including contraindicated self-management suggestions, potentially inappropriate dietary advice, and out-of-scope clinical instructions presented as self-care, indicating potential text-level safety concerns if used without professional review.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates multiple commercial LLMs on hemodialysis patient education questions for information quality, readability, and guideline consistency, but it does not test a specific deployment intervention or guardrail.
